note: Guide tones sung over a ii-V-I the backing track plays: the two written guide-tone lines on a staff with those notes ringed, then a line of the singer's own that starts each chord on a ringed note, with the rings following the chords. The chords are tokens counted the long way the first time, the key is moves (the second key of the old files), and the line about another key opens with {{?key}}.

exercise.title: Guide tones over ii-V-I
exercise.why: The 3rd and the 7th tell one chord from the next, and through a ii-V-I each of them moves a step or stays where it is, so a line made of them lets you hear every change.

cells.text: {{chord:ii7}} is the 2nd chord of the key, built on {{2}}. {{chord:V7}} is the 5th chord, built on {{5}}, and {{chord:Imaj7}} is the 1st, built on {{1}}.

Press Start exercise below: the mic and the backing track start together, with {{chord:Imaj7}} held for two bars. Sing one long note per chord: {{4}} over {{chord:ii7}}, {{4}} again over {{chord:V7}}, then {{3}} over {{chord:Imaj7}}. Sing it on "ah".
Then sing the other line: {{1}} over {{chord:ii7}}, {{7}} over {{chord:V7}}, {{7}} again over {{chord:Imaj7}}.
Listen for the bar where your note stays and the chord changes under it.
{{?key}}In another key the chords are new, and each line still stays for one change and moves one step down for the other.

Press Start exercise below to start the mic and the same chords. Make up your own line, and sing it on any vowel.
Start each chord on a ringed note: the rings move with the chords, and the tip under the staff names the notes. Leave space between phrases.
If you lose the chords, go back to one long ringed note per chord until you hear the changes again.
